## Why

The ui reported this as tool feedback (deterministic-check) on ork in ork run ork-20261118-130536-390b, project ork, item S398:
give doctor text output a golden test, so a UI pass can render the `[upgrade]` lines from a fixture without running the real binary or adding a test file
Evidence: TestDoctorUpgradeFlagPrintsEveryTool only checks substrings (internal/cli/upgrade_test.go:474-481); no golden file exists for doctor output, so no render could be produced for S398

Evidence (2026-11-18):

- `TestDoctorUpgradeFlagPrintsEveryTool` checks substrings and order only (`internal/cli/upgrade_test.go:467-487`); its unknown-source case reads the JSON (`internal/cli/upgrade_test.go:488-505`).
- The only golden views are the TUI's: `go test ./internal/tui -update` rewrites `testdata/golden/` (`internal/tui/golden_test.go:26-27`, AGENTS.md Project Commands). `internal/cli` has no golden file and no `-update` flag.
- The doctor fixtures put temp paths in the output (`env.adjPath`, `env.slicerD`, `internal/cli/upgrade_test.go:65-72`), so a golden must replace them with fixed words.

This slice touches `internal/cli` output tests and AGENTS.md's golden command; it gets a UI pass (rule u10). No product output changes.

## Implement

1. Write the failing tests and see them red for the stated reason.
2. `internal/cli/golden_test.go`: a package `-update` flag and a helper `golden(t, name, got)` that rewrites `testdata/golden/NAME` under `-update` and otherwise compares and prints a diff on mismatch, in the shape of `internal/tui/golden_test.go`.
3. A normalizer that replaces the env's temp paths (longest first) with the fixed words, so the files are the same on every host.
4. Run `go test ./internal/cli -update -run DoctorGolden` once, and review the three files: they are what a UI pass reads instead of running the binary.
5. Keep `TestDoctorUpgradeFlagPrintsEveryTool`; do not change doctor's output.
6. Docs: AGENTS.md Project Commands adds `go test ./internal/cli -update` beside the TUI line; `docs/design.md` doctor section names the goldens. Changelog entry with `slicer changelog add S434 --text "..."`.

## Check

Acceptance criteria:
- ork doctor text output, plain and with --upgrade for known and unknown sources, has golden files in testdata/golden.
- The golden files hold no host temp path, so they compare the same on every machine.
- The -update flag rewrites them; without it a change in doctor output fails the tests with a diff.
- No doctor output changes in this slice.
